title: LIBERO-MAX: Do Robot Policies Adapt When the World Changes?
abstract: arXiv:2609.36518v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robots must often continue a task after a target moves, the viewpoint shifts, or an obstacle appears, even though their earlier observations and committed actions reflect the previous scene. Many simulation robustness benchmarks fix external conditions at reset, leaving this temporal challenge underexamined. We introduce LIBERO-MAX, a benchmark of 8,000 paired cases spanning eight types of changes to geometry, observations, appearance, clutter, and paths. Each pair compares task execution with and without a mid-task event, holding the task, initial state, policy seed, and pre-event action sequence fixed. This controlled comparison distinguishes event-associated regressions from failures already present without the change. Across fourteen current VLA, hybrid, and world-action policies, events reduce success by 11.0-25.7 percentage points. translated_title: LIBERO-MAX：当世界变化时，机器人策略能否适应？
translated_abstract: 机器人在目标移动、视角改变或障碍物出现后，往往需要继续完成任务，即使其先前的观测和已执行的动作反映的是变化之前的场景。许多仿真鲁棒性基准在环境重置时固定外部条件，导致这一时间维度的挑战未得到充分研究。我们提出了LIBERO-MAX，一个包含8,000个配对案例的基准，涵盖几何、观测、外观、杂乱程度和路径方面的八种变化类型。每个配对案例在任务、初始状态、策略种子和事件前动作序列保持固定的条件下，比较任务在有与无任务中途事件时的执行表现。这种受控比较能够将事件引起的性能退化与原本就存在的失败区分开来。在十四个当前主流的VLA、混合以及世界-动作策略上，任务中途事件使成功率下降了11.0至25.7个百分点。事件剖析揭示了对几何和观测变化的共同脆弱性，而不同策略家……（摘要在此处不完整）
tldr: 该论文提出了LIBERO-MAX基准，通过8,000个受控配对案例系统评估机器人策略在任务中途遭遇环境变化（如目标移动、视角改变、障碍出现）时的适应能力，发现现有策略成功率下降11.0至25.7个百分点，并揭示出对几何和观测变化的共同脆弱性。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces LIBERO-MAX, a benchmark of 8,000 controlled paired cases that systematically evaluates how robot policies adapt to mid-task environmental changes, finding that current VLA, hybrid, and world-action policies suffer success drops of 11.0–25.7 percentage points with shared vulnerabilities to geometry and observation changes.
